intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

selected_hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Explore the medieval heart of Prague, wandering through Old Town Square and witnessing the iconic Astronomical Clock chime on the hour. Dive into centuries of Bohemian history with a self-guided or local-led walking tour through cobblestone streets, Gothic churches, and Baroque palaces.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in the grandeur of one of Europe's largest thermal bath complexes, built in 1913. Experience the healing mineral waters in stunning Neo-Baroque surroundings, a deeply rooted Budapest tradition that blends wellness, history, and local culture in one iconic setting.

experiences.name: Prague & Budapest Local Food Market Crawl
experiences.description: Sample authentic Central European cuisine across both cities — try trdelník and svíčková in Prague's Manifesto Market, then indulge in lángos, kürtőskalács, and chimney cake at Budapest's Great Market Hall. A delicious deep-dive into local flavors and street food culture.

experiences.name: Danube River Evening Cruise
experiences.description: Glide along the Danube at sunset and witness Budapest's illuminated skyline — the Parliament, Buda Castle, and Chain Bridge glowing against the night sky. This scenic cruise offers a breathtaking waterfront perspective of the city's UNESCO-listed panorama with optional wine and local snacks on board.

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex & Vltava Riverbank Walk
experiences.description: Spend a half-day exploring the world's largest ancient castle complex, including St. Vitus Cathedral and the Golden Lane. Afterward, stroll along the scenic Vltava riverbank promenade — the closest Prague gets to a waterfront experience — enjoying views of Charles Bridge and the city's historic skyline.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use morning for in-flight rest and preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Prague Airport at 13:00. Take Airport Express Bus (Line 119) to Nádraží Veleslavín metro station, then Metro Line A to Staroměstská stop (~45 min total, ~60 CZK). Check in to your Staré Město boutique stay. Once settled, take a gentle orientation stroll around Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí) — admire the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and Gothic Týn Church exterior. No need to rush; just absorb the medieval atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Wander across Charles Bridge at dusk for stunning golden-hour views of Prague Castle. The bridge is free and magical in the early evening light. Return to Old Town for a slow evening walk through the cobblestone lanes.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick snack at Prague Airport arrivals hall.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite near Old Town — try 'Lokál Dlouhááá' for a classic Czech open-faced sandwich (chlebíček, ~50–80 CZK) or pick up a fresh trdelník pastry from a street stall (~60 CZK) as a welcome snack while exploring.
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Restaurace U Provaznice' near Old Town — a no-frills Czech pub serving hearty svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings for ~180–250 CZK. Pair with a local Pilsner Urquell draft (~45 CZK).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light — you've just landed. Focus on orientation and rest. Exchange a small amount of currency (CZK) at the airport or use a fee-free card (Revolut/Wise). Avoid airport currency exchange booths with poor rates. Metro day pass costs ~120 CZK if you plan to travel more.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) exploration. Take Metro Line A to Malostranská, then walk uphill or take tram 22 to Pražský hrad stop. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral (free exterior, paid interior ~250 CZK for circuit ticket), Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane — a charming row of tiny medieval cottages. Arrive early (~9:00) to beat crowds. Budget ~3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) — explore the beautiful baroque Wallenstein Garden (free entry) and charming side streets. Cross Charles Bridge again in daylight to appreciate the 30 baroque statues up close. Head back to Old Town and visit the Old Town Hall Tower for panoramic rooftop views (~130 CZK). Browse the Havelské tržiště outdoor market for cheap souvenirs and fresh fruit.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) from the outside — walk past the Old Jewish Cemetery and synagogues (exterior free). Enjoy the atmospheric narrow streets at dusk. End the evening with a cold beer at a traditional Czech pivnice (pub).

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry and coffee at 'Café Louvre' or a local bakery near Old Town for ~80–120 CZK. Alternatively, pick up yogurt and fruit from a Billa or Albert supermarket (~40–60 CZK) for an ultra-budget start.
meals.lunch: Eat at 'Nase Maso' butcher-restaurant in Old Town — famous for affordable, quality Czech meat sandwiches and beef tartare (~120–180 CZK). Queue up and order at the counter.
meals.dinner: Try 'Pivnice U Zlatého Tygra' — a legendary Prague pub frequented by locals, serving simple Czech food and perfectly poured Pilsner Urquell. Dinner with beer ~200–280 CZK. Arrive early as it fills up fast.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is the largest ancient castle complex in the world — wear comfortable shoes. The full circuit ticket (~250 CZK) covers most key interiors. If budget is very tight, the castle courtyard and cathedral exterior are free. September weather in Prague is typically mild (15–20°C) — bring a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Vyšehrad Fortress — an often-overlooked gem. Take Metro Line C to Vyšehrad stop. Explore the free grounds, the stunning neo-Gothic Basilica of St. Peter and Paul (entry ~50 CZK), and the famous Slavín Cemetery where Czech luminaries like Dvořák and Mucha are buried. Enjoy panoramic views of the Vltava River from the ramparts. Far fewer tourists than Prague Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — two authentic, non-touristy Prague districts. Walk past beautiful Art Nouveau apartment buildings. Climb the Žižkov Television Tower (tallest building in Prague, ~230 CZK) for 360° city views and spot the famous crawling baby sculptures by David Černý. Explore the quirky local street art scene in Žižkov.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Town for a final evening stroll. Visit the Astronomical Clock for the hourly figure parade (best at 9 PM). Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the neighborhood before an early night — you have a travel day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Pick up supplies from a local supermarket (Albert on Náměstí Republiky) — bread, cheese, ham, and juice for ~60–80 CZK. Eat at your accommodation or in a park.
meals.lunch: Grab lunch in Vinohrady at 'Café Sladkovský' or any local Czech restaurant — look for 'denní menu' (daily lunch menu) boards offering soup + main course for ~150–180 CZK, a classic Czech budget lunch deal.
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Kantýna' — a popular Prague butcher-restaurant with quality Czech meats, salads, and craft beer at very reasonable prices (~200–280 CZK for a full meal). Great local atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Vinohrady and Žižkov are excellent for seeing how real Prague residents live, away from tourist traps. The Žižkov TV Tower is a polarizing but iconic piece of Czech architecture — worth the visit. Pack a light day bag with water and snacks. Tonight, pack your bags for the Budapest leg of the trip tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Prague accommodation early. Travel to Budapest by budget overnight or morning bus/train. The most affordable option is RegioJet or FlixBus (Prague to Budapest, ~€15–30, ~7–8 hours). Book in advance for best prices. Depart by 7:00–8:00 AM from Prague Florenc bus station (Metro Line B or C to Florenc). Enjoy the scenic Central European countryside en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest in the early-to-mid afternoon (~15:00–16:00). Check in to your Budapest accommodation. Take the metro or a bus to your neighborhood. Do a first orientation walk along the Danube riverbank on the Pest side — the view of Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, and the Parliament building across the water is breathtaking and completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Walk across the iconic Széchenyi Chain Bridge (free) to Buda side. Climb up to Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) for the most spectacular panoramic views of Budapest and the illuminated Parliament at sunset/dusk. The exterior terraces are free after 18:00 in September. Return to Pest for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick coffee and pastry at Prague Florenc bus station or bring snacks from the supermarket for the journey (~50–80 CZK / ~500–800 HUF).
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich or snacks for the bus journey to save money. Alternatively, RegioJet buses have a small café on board.
meals.dinner: First Budapest dinner at 'Frici Papa Kifőzdéje' — a legendary, no-frills Hungarian canteen in Pest serving authentic home-cooked Hungarian food (goulash, stuffed cabbage, chicken paprikash) for ~1,500–2,500 HUF (~€4–7). Beloved by locals.

day_by_day.notes: Travel day — keep it relaxed. RegioJet is highly recommended for comfort and price; book seats in advance online. Budapest uses Hungarian Forint (HUF). Withdraw cash from a bank ATM on arrival (avoid Euronet machines with poor rates). A 24-hour Budapest transport pass costs ~2,500 HUF (~€7) and covers metro, trams, and buses.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Buda Castle District (Várnegyed). Take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló, ~1,400 HUF one way) or hike up for free. Visit the exterior of Buda Castle (Royal Palace), the Hungarian National Gallery (free on certain days — check schedule), and the charming medieval streets of the Castle District. Visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom, ~3,000 HUF entry) with its stunning geometric Zsolnay tile roof.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Buda side and visit the Cave Church (Sziklatemplom) built into a cliff face (~700 HUF). Cross back to Pest via Chain Bridge. Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) — Budapest's most famous indoor market. Browse stalls of paprika, Hungarian sausages, lángos, and folk crafts. The ground floor is great for affordable local food.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the UNESCO-listed Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées equivalent. Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Millennium Monument (free). Walk through City Park (Városliget) as the sun sets. Return to the city center for a ruin bar experience in the Jewish Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese, ~600–900 HUF) from a street vendor near the Great Market Hall — an iconic Hungarian breakfast street food.
meals.lunch: Eat lunch inside the Great Market Hall — head to the upper floor food stalls for affordable Hungarian classics: goulash soup, stuffed peppers, or roasted duck leg (~1,500–2,500 HUF).
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Kádár Étkezde' in the Jewish Quarter — a legendary Budapest lunch-and-dinner spot with traditional Hungarian Jewish cuisine. Try the cholent or beef stew (~2,000–3,000 HUF). Cash only, very local atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means the Great Market Hall is busiest but also most vibrant. Arrive at the market before noon for the best experience. The ruin bars (romkocsmák) in the Jewish Quarter — especially Szimpla Kert — are a must-see Budapest cultural phenomenon. Szimpla Kert is free to enter and has affordable drinks (~700–1,200 HUF per beer).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the most beautiful Gothic Revival buildings in the world. Tours run regularly (~6,000 HUF for non-EU visitors, ~3,200 HUF for EU citizens — book online in advance). Afterward, walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) and see the powerful 'Shoes on the Danube Bank' Holocaust memorial (free). Visit St. Stephen's Basilica exterior and climb the dome for panoramic views (~800 HUF).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the famous Széchenyi Thermal Bath (Széchenyi Gyógyfürdő) — a quintessential Budapest experience. Entry with locker ~7,500–9,000 HUF (~€20–25). Spend 2–3 hours soaking in the outdoor and indoor thermal pools in a stunning neo-baroque setting. This is a genuine cultural experience, not just a tourist attraction.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Jewish Quarter (VII. District) — visit the Great Synagogue (Dohány Street Synagogue, largest in Europe, ~5,000 HUF) for its exterior and memorial garden, or just walk the atmospheric streets. Head into the ruin bar district for evening drinks and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Sunday morning at a local café — try 'Gerbeaud Cukrászda' on Vörösmarty Square for a splurge-worthy Hungarian pastry and coffee experience (~1,500–2,500 HUF). A Budapest institution since 1858.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap lunch before the baths — try a 'kifőzde' (Hungarian canteen) near the Széchenyi Bath in City Park, or pick up supplies from a Spar or Aldi supermarket (~800–1,200 HUF).
meals.dinner: Dinner at 'Menza' on Liszt Ferenc tér — a retro-styled Hungarian bistro with modern takes on classic dishes at mid-range prices (~2,500–4,000 HUF for a full meal). Great atmosphere on the lively pedestrian square.

day_by_day.notes: Book Parliament and Széchenyi Bath tickets online in advance, especially on Sunday when they can sell out. Bring flip-flops and a towel to the baths (or rent on-site for ~500–800 HUF extra). The Liszt Ferenc tér area is one of Budapest's best neighborhoods for evening dining and café culture.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Szentendre — a charming Serbian-influenced artist town on the Danube, 40 minutes from Budapest by HÉV suburban rail (from Batthyány tér, ~750 HUF each way). Explore the colorful baroque town center, Orthodox churches, and the Open-Air Ethnographic Museum (Skanzen, ~2,500 HUF) — one of the best folk museums in Central Europe showing traditional Hungarian village life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Szentendre's art galleries (many free or cheap), craft shops, and riverside promenade. Try marzipan treats at the famous Dobos Confectionery. Return to Budapest by mid-afternoon (~15:00). Visit the Budapest History Museum in Buda Castle (optional, ~2,000 HUF) or simply wander the Pest neighborhoods you haven't explored yet — try the VIII. District (Józsefváros) for authentic local life.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Danube — many budget operators offer 1-hour evening cruises from ~5,000–7,000 HUF, giving spectacular illuminated views of both banks, the bridges, and Parliament. Book online or at the Vigadó tér pier. Alternatively, watch the sunset from the free Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) viewpoint for a budget-friendly alternative.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your accommodation or grab a fresh pogácsa (savory cheese scone) and coffee from a local pékség (bakery) near your hotel for ~400–600 HUF.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Szentendre — try the local Serbian-Hungarian restaurant 'Aranysárkány' or any of the riverside restaurants. Look for the daily menu (napi menü) for a soup + main deal (~2,000–3,000 HUF).
meals.dinner: Final Budapest dinner at 'Bors GasztroBar' — a cult-favorite Budapest street food spot known for creative, gourmet-style soups and sandwiches at incredibly low prices (~1,200–2,000 HUF). Queue up — worth every minute of waiting.

day_by_day.notes: The HÉV to Szentendre is covered by a Budapest transport pass only within city limits — buy an extension ticket at Batthyány tér for the full journey (~750 HUF). Szentendre is most pleasant in the morning before day-trippers arrive. Gellért Hill is a 20–30 minute uphill walk from the Gellért tram stop but offers arguably the best free panorama in Budapest.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest. Visit any remaining sights — consider the Hungarian National Museum (Nemzeti Múzeum, ~1,600 HUF) for a deep dive into 1,000 years of Hungarian history, or revisit a favorite neighborhood for a final coffee and pastry. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at the Great Market Hall (paprika, pálinka, embroidered goods) — much cheaper than airport shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, head to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport. Take the 100E Airport Express bus from Deák Ferenc tér (~900 HUF, ~30–40 min). Arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before your flight. Use remaining HUF for a final Hungarian snack or coffee at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most beautiful and historically rich capitals.

meals.breakfast: A proper farewell Hungarian breakfast — visit 'New York Café' for the experience (coffee and pastry ~2,500–3,500 HUF) or keep it budget-friendly at a local bakery (~500–800 HUF). The New York Café is a splurge but one of the most beautiful café interiors in the world.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near your accommodation or at the Great Market Hall before heading to the airport. Keep it simple — a lángos or a quick canteen meal (~1,000–1,500 HUF).
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or in-flight meal depending on your departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Final budget summary estimate: Prague (3 nights + activities) ~€80–120 total; Budapest (4 nights + activities) ~€100–150 total; Prague–Budapest transport ~€20–30. Total 8-day trip budget estimate: ~€200–300 per person excluding flights and accommodation. Always carry some local cash as many traditional restaurants and markets are cash-only. Both Prague and Budapest are extremely safe for solo and group travelers.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town) via airport express bus or taxi (~45–60 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a hotel map and neighborhood walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll through Staré Město. Explore the iconic Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí), watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime on the hour, and admire the Church of Our Lady before Týn. Wander the cobblestone lanes nearby to soak in the medieval atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Charles Bridge at dusk for stunning golden-hour views of Prague Castle and the Vltava River. Explore the Malá Strana (Lesser Town) side briefly before heading back to Old Town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Café Louvre-style bistro near Old Town Square — try a Czech open-faced sandwich (chlebíček) and coffee at a local café like Café Savoy or a bakery on Dlouhá Street.
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33) — a beloved mid-range Czech gastropub. Order svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or roasted duck with red cabbage, paired with a glass of Pilsner Urquell on tap.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Prioritize getting your bearings and enjoying a relaxed first evening. September in Prague is mild (15–22°C), so a light jacket for the evening is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) visit — the largest ancient castle in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička). Book tickets online in advance to skip queues. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana's charming streets. Visit the Baroque St. Nicholas Church, then cross back over Charles Bridge (now less crowded than evenings). Head to the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — tour the Old Jewish Cemetery and one of the historic synagogues (Pinkas or Spanish Synagogue recommended).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Town for a relaxed evening. Browse the atmospheric streets around Týnská and Štupartská. Enjoy a classical music concert — Prague has nightly chamber concerts in historic churches and palaces (book via GoOut.net or directly at venues).

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or a nearby café — try a Czech breakfast with rye bread, cheese, and cold cuts at Café Nona or similar.
meals.lunch: Malá Strana lunch break at U Malé Velryby (The Little Whale) — cozy mid-range spot with Czech and European dishes. Budget ~350–500 CZK per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurace Mlejnec near Old Town — traditional Czech cuisine in a renovated mill setting. Try the pork knuckle (vepřové koleno) or goulash with bread dumplings. Budget ~400–600 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is best visited on a weekday morning to avoid weekend crowds. Josefov entry is separate from the castle — combined synagogue tickets cost ~350 CZK. Wear comfortable walking shoes — this is a very active day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Vyšehrad Fortress — a quieter, less touristy alternative to Prague Castle. Explore the neo-Gothic Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul, the Vyšehrad Cemetery (where Dvořák and Smetana are buried), and enjoy panoramic views of the Vltava River from the ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — Prague's trendy, local-feeling districts. Visit the quirky Žižkov Television Tower (with crawling baby sculptures by David Černý) and enjoy the bohemian café culture. Browse local vintage shops and independent bookstores.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Old Town, take a Prague Legends evening walking tour (many depart from Old Town Square) for ghost stories, history, and hidden courtyards. Alternatively, enjoy a riverside walk along Náplavka embankment where locals gather.

meals.breakfast: Eska Bakery (Pernerova 49, Karlín) — one of Prague's best artisan bakeries. Try sourdough pastries and excellent coffee. Worth the short tram ride.
meals.lunch: Manifesto Market (Žižkov) — a popular street food container market with diverse, affordable options. Great for trying local and international street food. Budget ~150–250 CZK.
meals.dinner: Café V Lese (Korunní 32, Vinohrady) — a charming neighborhood restaurant with seasonal Czech-European menu. Relaxed atmosphere, mid-range pricing. Budget ~400–550 CZK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is free to enter the grounds; the basilica and casemates have a small fee (~60 CZK). Tram lines 7 and 18 connect Vyšehrad to Old Town easily. This day gives a great taste of 'local Prague' beyond the tourist center.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Prague Municipal House (Obecní dům) — a stunning Art Nouveau masterpiece. Take a guided interior tour to see the Smetana Concert Hall and ornate rooms. Then explore nearby Náměstí Republiky and the Powder Gate (Prašná brána). Visit the Museum of Communism for a fascinating look at Czech 20th-century history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Take the RegioJet or FlixBus from Prague to Budapest (~7 hours by bus, or ~6.5 hours by train via Brno/Bratislava). Book in advance — trains depart from Praha hlavní nádraží (Main Train Station). Afternoon/evening arrival in Budapest.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Budapest (approximately 20:00–21:00). Check into your Budapest accommodation, freshen up, and take a short walk along the Danube riverbank near your hotel to get a first impression of the city lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a pekárna (Czech bakery) near Old Town for pastries and coffee before the journey.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch or grab food at Praha hlavní nádraží — try a trdelník pastry or a sandwich for the journey. Alternatively, RegioJet trains have a bistro car.
meals.dinner: Upon arrival in Budapest, try Belvárosi Lugas Étterem near the city center — a welcoming mid-range Hungarian restaurant. Order goulash soup (gulyásleves) and lángos (fried dough with sour cream and cheese) as a first taste of Hungary.

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague–Budapest transport at least 2–3 weeks in advance for best prices. RegioJet offers comfortable seats with free coffee — a pleasant journey. Alternatively, a flight (1h) is available but less scenic and less eco-friendly. Arriving in Budapest on Friday evening means the weekend atmosphere will be lively.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle District (Várnegyed) — take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up from Clark Ádám tér. Visit the Royal Palace (Hungarian National Gallery is inside), Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom), and the Fishermen's Bastion (Halászbástya) for breathtaking panoramic views of the Danube and Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Buda side and cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot to Pest. Explore the grand Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's answer to the Champs-Élysées. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House exterior (or book a guided interior tour if available). Browse the elegant shops and café terraces.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Great Market Hall area (Nagycsarnok) neighborhood. Join a Budapest ruin bar tour or discover the famous Szimpla Kert (Kazinczy u. 14) — the original ruin bar in the Jewish Quarter. A must-see Budapest cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Gerbeaud Café (Vörösmarty tér) — Budapest's most historic café since 1858. Splurge slightly on coffee and a slice of Dobos torte or Esterházy cake. Worth the experience.
meals.lunch: Borkonyha Winekitchen near St. Stephen's Basilica — Michelin-recommended but mid-range priced lunch menu. Or opt for a casual lángos from a street vendor near Fishermen's Bastion.
meals.dinner: Menza Restaurant (Liszt Ferenc tér 2) — stylish retro-Hungarian restaurant in the lively Liszt Ferenc Square. Excellent gulyás, stuffed peppers, and Hungarian wines. Budget ~4,500–7,000 HUF per person.

day_by_day.notes: Fishermen's Bastion is free to walk around (the upper terraces have a small fee). Saturday in Budapest is lively — Szimpla Kert is busiest but most atmospheric on weekends. Wear comfortable shoes for the Buda Castle cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Thermal bath experience at Széchenyi Thermal Bath (Széchenyi gyógyfürdő) in City Park — one of Europe's largest and most beautiful spa complexes. Soak in the outdoor pools, try steam rooms and saunas. Book tickets online in advance (~6,000–8,000 HUF). Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) and Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) — a grand millennium monument with statues of Hungarian chieftains and kings. Visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) for European masterworks, or the interactive House of Music Hungary (new landmark building by Sou Fujimoto).
day_by_day.evening: Danube River Cruise at sunset — take a 1-hour sightseeing cruise departing from Vigadó tér or Batthyány tér. Spectacular views of the illuminated Parliament Building, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle. Book with Legenda or Mahart PassNave (~4,000–6,000 HUF).

meals.breakfast: Local Sunday market breakfast — try the Fény utcai Piac market in Buda (open Sunday mornings) for fresh produce, langos, and local cheeses. Alternatively, a café near your hotel.
meals.lunch: Bring a picnic to City Park, or dine at Robinson Restaurant on the lake island in City Park — mid-range Hungarian cuisine in a beautiful setting.
meals.dinner: Karavan Street Food (Kazinczy u. 18, Jewish Quarter) — an outdoor street food court next to Szimpla Kert. Try chimney cake (kürtőskalács), pulled pork, and craft beers. Casual, affordable, and very popular with locals and travelers alike.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a good day for thermal baths as locals visit too — arrive early (before 10:00) to secure a locker. The Danube cruise is best booked 1–2 days ahead in September. Bring sunscreen — September sun can still be strong in Budapest.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of Europe's most magnificent Neo-Gothic buildings. Book an interior guided tour in advance (mandatory, ~8,000 HUF). The tour includes the Crown Jewels and the grand staircase. Exterior views from the Danube embankment are equally spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jewish Quarter (VII. District) in depth — visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga), the largest in Europe. Tour the Hungarian Jewish Museum and Memorial Garden. Then wander the trendy ruin bar district streets (Kazinczy, Rumbach, Kertész utca) for street art and café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) for the best panoramic views of Budapest at golden hour and dusk. Hike up (30 min) or take a taxi to the Citadella fortress. Watch the city light up below. Descend via the cave church on the hillside.

meals.breakfast: New York Café (Erzsébet krt. 9-11) — dubbed 'the most beautiful café in the world.' A slight splurge for the experience; try coffee and a pastry in the gilded interior.
meals.lunch: Hummus Bar (multiple locations in the Jewish Quarter) — excellent Middle Eastern food, very popular with locals. Affordable and filling. Budget ~2,000–3,000 HUF.
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown or Borkonyha (mid-range fine dining) — treat yourself to an elevated Hungarian-European dinner on your last full Budapest evening. Alternatively, Rézkakas Bistro on Dohány Street for classic Hungarian dishes in a warm setting. Budget ~6,000–10,000 HUF.

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online at jegymester.hu — very popular and often sold out days in advance. Gellért Hill is free to walk up and worth every step for the views. Monday is a good day for museums as they're less crowded than weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit St. Stephen's Basilica (Szent István Bazilika) for free entry to the main nave, or pay ~500 HUF to climb the dome for city views. Browse the surrounding Zrinyi Street for souvenir shopping — pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, Unicum herbal liqueur, or handmade crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Central Market Hall (Nagycsarnok, Fővám tér) — Budapest's magnificent 19th-century iron-and-tile market. Ground floor has fresh produce, meats, and cheeses; upper floor has folk art, embroidery, and affordable souvenirs. Perfect for last-minute gifts and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (BUD) for departure. Allow 60–90 minutes for the journey from the city center (Airport Shuttle or taxi recommended). Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most magnificent capitals.

meals.breakfast: Café Frei (multiple locations) or August Cukrászda — a beloved Budapest patisserie. Try a rétes (Hungarian strudel) with apple or cherry filling and a coffee.
meals.lunch: Last Hungarian meal at the Great Market Hall — grab a plate of stuffed cabbage (töltött káposzta) or goulash from the upper-floor food stalls. Affordable and authentically local. Budget ~2,000–3,500 HUF.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or a light snack before boarding — or dine early at a restaurant near your hotel before heading to the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Budapest Airport is ~30 km from the city center. The 100E airport bus (350 HUF) runs to Deák Ferenc tér but only in one direction. For departure, use Minibud shuttle (~8,000 HUF) or taxi (~8,000–12,000 HUF). Allow extra time for Monday/Tuesday morning traffic. Pack Tokaji Aszú wine carefully — it's a perfect edible souvenir from Hungary.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged via luxury car service (Mercedes E-Class or similar) to boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Staré Město. Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge, admire the Baroque statues, and soak in your first views of Prague Castle across the Vltava River. Continue into Old Town Square to see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the Gothic Church of Our Lady before Týn. Keep the pace relaxed after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Evening cocktails at a rooftop bar in Old Town (Terasa U Prince offers sweeping views of the Astronomical Clock). Follow with a welcome dinner at a top Prague restaurant to ease into the local food scene.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: Light arrival bite at the hotel or a nearby café in Staré Město, such as Café Savoy (Viennese-style grand café with premium pastries and open sandwiches)
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — Michelin-starred Czech tasting menu celebrating traditional Bohemian ingredients elevated to fine dining; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Flight lands at 13:00 — factor in ~45 minutes immigration/baggage and ~30–40 minutes transfer. Realistically at hotel by 14:30–15:00. Keep Day 1 light and walkable. September in Prague is mild (15–22°C), ideal for evening strolls.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex exploration. Arrive early (~9:00) to beat crowds. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral (Gothic masterpiece), the Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane. Hire a licensed private guide for 2–3 hours for rich historical context on Bohemian kings, Habsburg rule, and Czech statehood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) — explore the Baroque St. Nicholas Church and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the Wallenstein Palace Garden, one of Prague's most stunning Baroque gardens. Cross back over Charles Bridge at leisure, browsing the artisan stalls. Optional: visit the Franz Kafka Museum for literary and cultural depth.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague is world-renowned for chamber music; opt for a performance at the Estates Theatre (Mozart conducted Don Giovanni here in 1787) or the Municipal House (Art Nouveau masterpiece). Book premium seats in advance.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Café Louvre — a historic 1902 grand café frequented by Kafka and Einstein, serving Central European breakfast classics
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá — celebrated Czech gastropub in Old Town serving perfectly poured Pilsner Urquell tank beer and elevated traditional dishes like svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce)
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant — modern Czech cuisine using hyper-local and seasonal ingredients; intimate, design-forward space in Old Town

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is the largest ancient castle complex in the world — wear comfortable shoes. Book concert tickets at least 2–3 days ahead. The Estates Theatre is a 5-minute walk from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Jewish Quarter (Josefov) deep-dive. Explore the UNESCO-listed Jewish Quarter — visit the Old Jewish Cemetery (one of Europe's oldest), the Pinkas Synagogue (memorial to Holocaust victims), the Spanish Synagogue (stunning Moorish Revival interior), and the Old-New Synagogue (Gothic, 13th century). A private guide adds invaluable historical and cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha, then explore the upscale Pařížská Boulevard (Paris Street) — Prague's most luxurious shopping avenue lined with Hermès, Louis Vuitton, and Dior. Alternatively, browse premium Czech crystal and garnets at Moser or Granat Turnov flagship stores.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Vltava River cruise — book a private or small-group premium dinner cruise along the river for golden-hour views of Prague's skyline, bridges, and illuminated castle. Champagne on deck as the city lights up.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Eska — award-winning bakery and restaurant in Karlín district, known for sourdough bread, natural wines, and seasonal Czech produce
meals.lunch: Café Imperial — stunning Art Deco interior with original 1914 ceramic tile mosaics; serves refined Czech and Central European cuisine
meals.dinner: Private dinner cruise on the Vltava — curated 3-course menu with local Czech wines and panoramic views of the illuminated city

day_by_day.notes: Josefov admission is a combined ticket covering 6 synagogues and the cemetery — purchase online to skip queues. The Jewish Quarter is a 10-minute walk from the hotel. Pařížská Street is immediately adjacent to Josefov.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora (~1.5 hours from Prague by private transfer). Visit the hauntingly beautiful Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) — a medieval chapel decorated with the bones of 40,000 people, a uniquely macabre and historically rich experience. Continue to the stunning Gothic Cathedral of St. Barbara, a UNESCO World Heritage Site rivaling Prague's St. Vitus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kutná Hora's medieval silver mining heritage at the Czech Museum of Silver and the Hrádek. The town was once one of the wealthiest in Central Europe due to its silver mines. Return to Prague by private car by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Old Town — explore the atmospheric narrow lanes around Týn Courtyard (Ungelt), browse independent boutiques, and enjoy a pre-dinner aperitif at a wine bar specializing in Moravian wines.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Pivnice Dačický — a historic pub in a 16th-century building serving traditional Czech cuisine in an authentic setting
meals.dinner: Aromi — acclaimed Italian-Czech fusion restaurant in Prague's Vinohrady neighborhood; exceptional wine list and seasonal tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: Private car hire for Kutná Hora day trip is strongly recommended for flexibility and comfort (~3,000–4,000 CZK round trip). Book Sedlec Ossuary tickets online in advance. Return to Prague by 17:00 to freshen up before dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer day: Prague to Budapest by luxury private transfer or first-class train (Railjet, ~6.5 hours) or premium flight (~1.5 hours). If taking the scenic train, enjoy the Central European countryside. Arrive in Budapest mid-morning to early afternoon depending on chosen transport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into luxury Budapest hotel (recommended: Four Seasons Gresham Palace or Aria Hotel Budapest). After settling in, take a first walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) and admire the Buda Castle Hill across the river. Explore the Inner City (Belváros) and the iconic Chain Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome evening in Budapest — visit the rooftop bar at 360 Bar (Opera House rooftop) for panoramic views of the city at sunset. Dine in style to celebrate your arrival in the Hungarian capital.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Prague before departure or café at Prague Main Station
meals.lunch: On-board dining if taking the Railjet train (dining car available), or airport lounge dining if flying
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown — Budapest's Michelin-starred restaurant on the Danube bank; Hungarian ingredients with contemporary European technique and outstanding wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book transport Prague–Budapest well in advance. Railjet first class is scenic and comfortable; flying is faster but adds airport time. The Four Seasons Gresham Palace is a restored Art Nouveau masterpiece directly on the Chain Bridge — an iconic Budapest stay. September is peak season in Budapest; book all reservations ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Buda Castle Hill exploration. Cross the Chain Bridge and ascend to Castle Hill via the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló). Visit the Royal Palace (Hungarian National Gallery and Budapest History Museum), the Matthias Church (stunning Neo-Gothic with Zsolnay ceramic roof tiles), and the Fisherman's Bastion for panoramic views over the Danube, Parliament, and Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to explore the Cave Church (Sziklatemplom) carved into the castle hill rock face, then visit Gellért Hill and the Citadella for sweeping city views. Return to Pest via the Liberty Bridge. Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's largest and most atmospheric covered market — for local paprika, Tokaji wine, foie gras, and Hungarian crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Thermal bath experience at the legendary Széchenyi Baths or the Art Nouveau Gellért Baths — book a private cabin or premium evening session. Follow with dinner at a prestigious Hungarian restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or New York Café — arguably the world's most beautiful café (opened 1894), serving lavish Hungarian breakfasts under gilded Neo-Baroque ceilings
meals.lunch: Borkonyha Winekitchen — Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant in the Jewish Quarter; exceptional Hungarian wines paired with creative seasonal dishes
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant — two Michelin stars; elegant Hungarian haute cuisine in a stunning space near Vörösmarty Square; one of Budapest's finest dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Fisherman's Bastion is free to access (towers have a small fee). Széchenyi Baths are the largest in Budapest; book private cabin (cabin privé) for a premium experience. Great Market Hall is closed Sundays — substitute with a stroll through the Váci Street area or the Hold Street Market.

day_by_day.morning: Hungarian Parliament Building — book a premium guided tour of the magnificent Neo-Gothic Parliament (third largest in the world), including the Hungarian Crown Jewels and the Holy Crown of St. Stephen. Afterward, walk along the UNESCO-listed Danube Promenade and visit the poignant Shoes on the Danube Bank Holocaust memorial.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Jewish Quarter (VII. District) — visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (largest in Europe), the adjacent Jewish Museum, and the Emanuel Tree memorial. Wander through the Ruin Bar district (romkocsmák) — Budapest's unique cultural phenomenon of bars built in abandoned buildings; visit Szimpla Kert (the original) even during the day for its eclectic atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Danube River dinner cruise — book a premium evening cruise with a 4–5 course Hungarian dinner, live folk or classical music, and champagne as you glide past illuminated landmarks including the Parliament, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most historic patisserie (est. 1858); enjoy Hungarian cakes, strudels, and light lunch dishes in grand surroundings
meals.dinner: Premium Danube dinner cruise — curated Hungarian menu featuring dishes like gulyás, foie gras, and Dobos torte dessert, paired with Tokaji Aszú and Egri Bikavér wines

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked online in advance — English tours fill up quickly, especially on weekends. The Great Synagogue charges entry; book online. Evening cruise typically departs from Vigadó Square, a 5-minute walk from most central hotels.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Hungarian State Opera House for a guided tour of the stunning Neo-Renaissance interior (one of the most beautiful opera houses in Europe). If time allows, explore Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées, UNESCO-listed) and the House of Terror Museum for a sobering and important look at Hungary's 20th-century history under Nazi and Soviet regimes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure time for last-minute luxury shopping along Andrássy Avenue (Prada, Gucci, local designers) or a final visit to a thermal spa. Enjoy a farewell Hungarian coffee and pastry at Auguszt Cukrászda or Ruszwurm Confectionery (Budapest's oldest, est. 1827, on Castle Hill). Private transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — flight home or onward destination. Carry the memories of two of Central Europe's most magnificent capitals.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final hotel breakfast — savor it
meals.lunch: Stand25 Bisztró — beloved Budapest bistro known for its refined Hungarian comfort food, excellent natural wines, and warm atmosphere; perfect farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight — consider purchasing Tokaji Aszú wine and Hungarian salami from the airport duty-free as edible souvenirs

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure from Budapest Airport. Private airport transfer recommended. Consider packing Tokaji wine, Hungarian paprika, Unicum liqueur, and Zsolnay porcelain as premium souvenirs. This trip covers approximately 8 days of premium cultural immersion across two extraordinary Central European capitals.
